conviction_note: The print turns on the first outlook that includes Airtable (closed 2026-09-04) and Miro (closed 2026-10-26). The company said it will add Miro to its outlook at this print, and adding both mechanically lifts FY26 revenue from the $2.78-2.82B ex-M&A guide to roughly $3.0B+, against a Street average of $2.9B. Against that: the only confirmed public-company print (Q2, 2026-08-13) was a beat that closed -16.5% on a FY guide below the Street; the options show heavy put skew (+13.6 vol pts, P/C OI 4.33); and the acquired businesses dilute margin while about $3.5B of new debt dilutes EPS. Net, a mild up-lean: p_up 55 on an abs move of 15 gives +1.5. The findings sum to +2.6; the gap is the skew and the reaction function, which I let pull p_up toward 50 rather than shrinking the findings twice.

findings.finding: The FY26 outlook will be re-issued including Airtable (~$480M ARR, closed 2026-09-04) and Miro (~$600M ARR, closed 2026-10-26), which the $2.78-2.82B guide excluded; the company said it will add Miro to the outlook at this print. The arithmetic: the ex-M&A midpoint of $2.80B, plus an Airtable Q3 stub (~$30-35M), a full Airtable Q4 (~$120M) and ~66 days of Miro (~$105M), gives roughly $3.0-3.06B. Against the FY Street average of $2.9B (range $2.8-3.06B) that is a headline raise, closing the 'full-year gap' the preview framed as the debate.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The FY guide line drove the only confirmed print: on 2026-08-13 a FY midpoint $95M below the Street took the stock -16.46% close-to-close despite a revenue and EPS beat (baseline; https://finviz.com/news/381910/bending-spoons-shares-slip-despite-q2-earnings-and-revenue-beat).
findings.why_not_priced: If the market priced the mechanical lift, Q4 estimates would cluster near $950-980M, and the preview would not still be framing a FY gap the Street has not closed. Instead Q4 consensus averages $866M with a $755-977M range, so some models are ex-M&A, and the 25d skew still pays +13.6 vol points for downside. The partial offset: FY2027 Street at $4.26B shows many models already carry the acquisitions, so the 'beat' versus the average partly reflects stale ex-M&A models.

findings.finding: Q3 reported revenue includes ~27 days of Airtable (closed 2026-09-04, ~$480M ARR, roughly $30-35M), which the $733-745M Q3 guide excluded. Consensus ($740.3M finviz, $741.1M Benzinga, $746.4M Yahoo avg) sits at the guide midpoint, so revenue should print ~$765-775M, about 3-4% above the bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2's revenue beat of +2.8% ($704M vs $685M) was sold, -16.46% close-to-close, because the guide disappointed. The holders look through reported-quarter revenue, especially acquired revenue (organic was 3%).
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus at the guide midpoint ($740M), and a Yahoo high of $774.5M, suggest most models did not add the stub. But the market treats acquired revenue as known and will strip it out.
findings.independence: The Q3 guide excluded acquisitions (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0002004711/000200471126000011/bsp_ex99-1.htm). This shares the Airtable close fact with the guide finding but lands on a different line (Q3 reported versus FY outlook).

findings.finding: BofA, an Underperform holder of the bear case, wrote on 2026-11-16 that investor expectations for Q3 revenue have fallen 'significantly' below management's guidance, and that Q3 organic growth carries mild upside risk. That puts the buy-side bar below the $740M sell-side consensus, while BofA itself sees no data showing AI-agent-driven cancellations at scale.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior instance: there is only one confirmed print. At Q2 the buy side expected a FY midpoint at the Street, and the gap below it drove -16.5%.
findings.why_not_priced: This is what the low bar looks like in the price: -12% since the last report, -6.35% over 20 days, and heavy put demand. What has not been tested is that the bar is low, so even an in-line guide plus the M&A lift clears it. The sell-side consensus does not show this bar; only a bearish broker's note does.
findings.independence: Fortune 2026-11-17 reports the same BofA note: 'organic growth has mild upside risk' for Q3, and the company spokesperson saw no AI-driven cancellations (https://fortune.com/2026/11/17/ai-agents-b2a-bending-spoons-ubs-bofa-subscriptions/). Same underlying note, so one source.

findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-10-14: Berkshire's $330M placement news squeezed the stock +35% intraday, which shows how hard the name gaps on a positive surprise with this short base (https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/10/14/why-bending-spoons-stock-popped-today).
findings.why_not_priced: The skew itself is the market saying downside is more likely, which is the side this finding argues against. It is filed because 8 days to cover on a lock-up-constrained float is a squeeze mechanism if the guide lifts. If the squeeze risk were priced, call skew would be bid rather than puts.

findings.finding: The only confirmed earnings print as a public company sold a clean beat hard. On 2026-08-13, revenue beat by +2.8%, adj. EPS by 70% ($0.46 vs $0.27), and Q3 revenue was guided in line, yet the stock closed -16.46% because the FY midpoint ($2.80B) sat below the Street ($2.895B) and organic growth was 3%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This is the reaction history itself. The other baseline rows (2026-07-28, 09-04, 09-10, 10-26) are deal and closing announcements, not prints.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a reaction function, not a fact the market lacks. It says holders price organic growth and the quality of the guide, not the acquired top line, which cuts against the mechanical-raise finding.

findings.finding: Margin and EPS dilution in the new outlook. Airtable and Miro were growth-stage businesses bought at ~2.3-2.7x ARR, so they will dilute the 54% adj. operating margin before the cost cuts land. New debt adds interest: a $1.25B + EUR395M term-loan add-on (2026-09-25) and $1.25B + EUR500M senior secured notes (2026-10-28), about $3.5B in total. Consensus FY26 EPS has drifted down from $1.42 to $1.37 over 90 days.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None isolated. The Q2 EPS beat (+70%) did not help the stock, so EPS and margin have so far been secondary to the revenue guide.
findings.why_not_priced: The EPS trend down and BofA's 2026-2028 EPS cuts show it is partly priced. The size of the adj. OI margin step-down in the FY guide is not visible until the outlook is given.

findings.finding: The new debt was raised to buy recurring revenue, not out of distress. The term-loan add-on funded Miro and was upsized from a $750M target to $1.25B, with Moody's upgrading to Ba3 and S&P to BB-. The notes, upsized from $1.5B to ~$1.8B, fund unnamed future acquisitions. Leverage was 2.4x at Q2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Deal and financing days: Miro agreement 2026-09-10 +5.09%, Miro close 2026-10-26 +5.78% (baseline). BofA's August downgrade argued the price implies ~$18B of M&A versus ~$7B of debt capacity (https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-bending-spoons-bsp-stock-down-9-02-today-15611/).
findings.why_not_priced: The financing is public. The question the print answers is whether the leverage target and the M&A pipeline commentary reassure, which is two-sided, so it is sized at 0.

findings.finding: BofA (2026-11-16) rates about 29% of projected 2027 revenue as high AI-agent risk (AOL $778.8M, Eventbrite $403.1M, Evernote $125.5M). Hedgeye (short since 2026-07-24) argues most growth is bought and the core assets are mature or declining. Q2 organic growth was 3%, so any organic slip in Q3 gives this narrative a number.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The BofA downgrade on 2026-08-11 coincided with -9.0% in a day, after a +52% 5-session run (https://tickeron.com/blogs/why-is-bending-spoons-bsp-stock-down-9-02-today-15611/).
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: it is published and the put skew reflects it. BofA itself expects the big hit in 2-3 years, not this quarter, and sees mild upside to Q3 organic growth. The residual is the risk that organic growth turns negative.
findings.independence: Hedgeye note: https://longbridge.com/news/293760561 (2026-07-24). This shares the BofA note with the buy-side-bar finding (one document, two lines: the AI-risk view here, the expectations bar there).

findings.finding: BSP laid off a large part of Airtable's team in mid-October (announced 2026-10-12; ~190 per a WARN-based tracker). This is its usual post-deal cost reset, which supports the Q4 adjusted operating income contribution from Airtable despite the margin dilution.
findings.why_not_priced: Headcount is undisclosed, so the analysts' Q4 adj. OI cannot carry a number for it until management gives the integrated outlook.

findings.finding: Adj. EPS bar looks low against the guide. Q3 adj. operating income is guided at $380-400M, flat to up on Q2's $381M, which produced $0.46 adj. EPS. EPS consensus is $0.26-0.31 (disputed across finviz, Yahoo and Benzinga), and estimates were 70% too low last quarter. Higher interest and IPO shares cut the gap but likely do not close it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 adj. EPS beat by $0.19 (+70%) and the stock fell 16.5%. EPS beats do not move this name.
findings.why_not_priced: Revisions were 5 up and 1 down over 30 days, so the bar is moving up. Capped small because the bar is disputed across sources.

baseline_tension: The findings lean up (a mechanical FY raise from consolidating acquisitions, plus a buy-side bar below guidance) against a strong put skew (+13.6) and a reaction history where the only print sold a beat by 16.5%. I hold the skew wrong only to the extent that the inclusion of Airtable and Miro is mechanical and was promised, so p_up is kept at 55 rather than higher.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 (verified fact is not a reaction): the Q3 revenue stub finding went from +1.0 to +0.5 and the EPS finding from +0.5 to +0.3, because the only print sold a beat by 16.5%.

Rule 7 (positioning, skew): the guide-raise finding went from +3.0 to +2.5, because its sign is against a +13.6 skew; the stated reason the option market may be wrong is that the inclusion of acquisitions is mechanical and promised. p_up went from 56 to 55.

Rule 3 / one document counted once: the BofA buy-side-bar finding went from +2.0 to +1.5, because it rests on a single bearish broker's note that also feeds the AI-risk finding. The draft's separate Hedgeye finding (-0.2) was merged into the AI-risk finding as the same concern.
History lesson for foreign private issuers: the base rate was rebuilt from the one confirmed release (2026-08-13, -16.46%); the other baseline rows are deal announcements.
Rule 6 (bar): EPS findings stay capped small because the EPS bar is disputed ($0.26/$0.30/$0.31); the revenue bar has two agreeing sources (~$740-741M) plus Yahoo's $746M.
Rule 4 (financing): the financing stays at 0 after asking what the money buys (Miro, a ratings upgrade, future M&A).
